title: Jim Tatum's Only Season at Oklahoma: The 1946 Sooners
question: Who coached Oklahoma football in 1946, right before Bud Wilkinson?
answer: Jim Tatum coached Oklahoma for one season, 1946, going 8-3, sharing the Big Six title and beating NC State 34-13 in the Gator Bowl on Jan. 1, 1947. He then left for Maryland, and his assistant Bud Wilkinson took over.
summary: Jim Tatum coached OU for just the 1946 season, went 8-3, shared the Big Six title and won the Gator Bowl before leaving for Maryland and Bud Wilkinson.
body: The coach who handed the keys to Bud Wilkinson only stayed one year. Jim Tatum ran the Oklahoma program in 1946, the first season after World War II, and in that single fall he put together an 8-3 record, a 4-1 mark in the Big Six Conference and a share of the league title with Kansas.

Tatum came to Norman with ties to the split-T. He had been an assistant to Don Faurot, the formation's creator, at the Navy's Iowa Pre-Flight program, and he had already been a head coach at his alma mater, North Carolina, in 1942. He also brought in Bud Wilkinson, a former Minnesota star he had worked alongside at Iowa Pre-Flight, as his backfield coach.

The 1946 Sooners finished No. 14 in the final AP poll and closed the season in Jacksonville, Florida, beating No. 18 NC State 34-13 in the Gator Bowl on New Year's Day 1947. Back Joe Golding, who ran for 902 yards that year, was named the game's MVP. Guards Plato Andros and Buddy Burris and center John Rapacz earned first-team All-America honors.

Then Tatum was gone, hired by Maryland after the season. OU promoted Wilkinson, then 31, to head coach and athletic director, and the rest is Sooner history. Tatum went on to coach Maryland and later returned to North Carolina, finishing his career 100-35-7. The College Football Hall of Fame inducted him in 1984, which means OU's one-year coach is one of six Sooner head coaches enshrined there for their coaching.
